title: Premium
exclusionReason: No side-view camera available (standard or optional)
infotainment: 12.3-inch landscape touchscreen with wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, embedded navigation, OTA-updateable
adasStandard: Subaru EyeSight Driver Assist Technology suite standard on all Solterra trims: Pre-Collision Braking, Pre-Collision Throttle Management, Lane Departure Warning, Lane Departure Prevention, Lane Centering Function, Adaptive Cruise Control with full-stop, Lead Vehicle Start Alert, Sway Warning, Emergency Steering Assist, Intersection Collision Avoidance Support, DriverFocus Distraction Mitigation, Emergency Driving Stop System, Hands-Free Low Speed Driving (Traffic Jam Assist). Also standard: Blind Spot Detection, Rear Cross-Traffic Alert, Auto-Reverse Braking, Front-View Monitor camera. Source: https://www.subaru.com/vehicles/solterra/2025.html
adasOptional: No additional ADAS hardware options on Premium beyond the standard EyeSight suite.
rearViewCameraNotes: Standard rearview camera with dynamic guidelines. Subject of NHTSA recall on early 2023-2024 cars (camera freeze on reverse); addressed via software update [https://recharged.com/articles/subaru-solterra-recalls-list]. Multi-angle features arrive on higher trims via Front-View Monitor.
sideViewCameraNotes: No surround-view 360 camera standard on Premium; available on Limited/Touring (Subaru Panoramic View Monitor). No Honda-LaneWatch-style side camera on Subaru.
subscriptionFeatures: STARLINK Safety Plus (automatic collision notification, SOS, enhanced roadside assistance) and Security Plus (remote start, remote lock/unlock, stolen vehicle recovery, geofencing alerts) are subscription packages. Pricing typically $99/yr for Safety Plus, $149/yr for Security Plus after a 1-3 year trial. Heated seats, ADAS, and powertrain features are NOT subscription-gated on this trim. SiriusXM trial included.
drmNotes: Vehicle operates fully offline for core driving. STARLINK connected services (Safety Plus / Security Plus packages) require active subscription after trial. OTA software updates flow via Toyota/Subaru infrastructure (Solterra shares Toyota platform). No documented history of post-sale feature reduction by Subaru. Source: https://www.subaru.com/subaru-starlink/starlink-safety-and-security.html
killSwitchNotes: No impaired-driving kill switch implemented. DriverFocus camera-based distraction monitor on this trim warns the driver but does not disable the vehicle. Subaru has not publicly announced a federal-mandate kill-switch implementation timeline.
knownIssues: 2023-2024 model years had wheel-hub-bolt recall (potential wheel detachment), HVAC failsafe mode disabling heater/defroster, and rearview camera freeze recall. MY2025 has had 2 NHTSA recalls; pattern indicates ongoing software/electrical quality issues on the shared Subaru/Toyota platform. Source: https://recharged.com/articles/subaru-solterra-recalls-list
recalls: MY2025 Solterra: 2 NHTSA recalls as of mid-2026. See https://www.cars.com/research/subaru-solterra/recalls/ for the live list.
stateIncentives: Solterra was assembled in Japan and historically did not qualify for the federal 30D new-purchase tax credit. The $7,500 commercial-clean-vehicle credit was applied to leases through Subaru Motors Finance until 9/30/2025 [https://www.camelbacksubaru.com/blog/2025/july/16/federal-ev-tax-credit-home-charger-incentive-changes.htm]. State incentives vary widely (CA CVRP, CO tax credit, NY Drive Clean Rebate, NJ Charge Up, etc.).
